bib.title: Learning to Reason and Memorize with Self-Notes
bib.venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)

question: Can a language model reason and keep state better by writing notes interleaved with the context as it reads, rather than only after reading the whole context as in scratchpad or chain-of-thought?
hypothesis: Interleaving reasoning with the input context puts reasoning closer to relevant facts and acts as recurrent working memory, so it generalises better than post-context scratchpad/CoT.
contributions: Self-Notes: model may deviate from the context at any time (start token) to write a note that is appended in place
Four learning paradigms: supervised, semi-supervised, unsupervised, few-shot prompted
New synthetic Toy-Story task; experiments on 7 datasets

method.summary: The LM generates note tokens inline whenever the next token is in a start-token set; notes end at an end token or a fixed length and are inserted into the context before reading continues. Trained (GPT-2 fine-tuning) or prompted (GPT-J, GPT-3, Llama 2) and compared to Vanilla and Scratchpad/CoT.
method.task: multi-step reasoning and state tracking in text (synthetic, chess, math word problems)

datasets.name: Toy-Story
datasets.split: train 1-2 hop; test in-domain 1/2-hop, OOD 3 and 4-hop

datasets.name: Algorithmic
datasets.source: Algorithmic task adopted from reference [11] of the paper
datasets.preprocessing: input and label tokens unified into one sequence

datasets.name: Chess Piecetype
datasets.preprocessing: moves split c2c4 to c2 c4; 64 board squares added to vocabulary

datasets.name: MultiArith
datasets.source: Roy and Roth [18]; prompts from Wei et al.

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.preprocessing: calculation annotations in << >> removed for CoT

other.access: OpenAI API, no token probabilities over prompt

training.objective: standard LM loss on context and answer tokens (Vanilla, Self-Notes); Scratchpad trained on context+answer for Toy-Story, answer only for other tasks
training.regularisation: random offset of positional embedding IDs in 0-128 during training for length-generalisation tasks

other.semi_supervised: samples without notes get a special prefix token s
other.unsupervised: train on varying-length QA, test-time notes are model-generated questions with answers inserted; start token boosted by B=5; multi-sample then pick most confident; then finetune on note-enriched data

inference.samples: mean ± std reported in Table 2; number of runs not stated; unsupervised multi-sample count not stated
inference.prompting: few-shot: MultiArith 8-shot (Wei et al.), GSM8K 5-shot, Algorithmic 5-shot (6-33 statements); notes in parentheses inline; Llama 2 uses the 8-shot Wei prompt

parameters.start_tokens: Algorithmic/Boolean ' print', end ' ;'; chess: piece tokens, no end token; math: start ' (' end ')'; Toy-Story: 'SQ:'
parameters.api_note_positions: GPT-3 notes allowed only after '.', ',' or '?'

eval.protocol: in-distribution and OOD test sets; mean ± std; no validation set for prompting

prompts.text:
Q: If there are 3 cars in the parking lot and 2 more cars arrive, (3 + 2 = 5 total) how many cars are in the parking lot?
A: The answer is 5.

evidence.quote: we train for a fixed 30 epochs with a learning rate of 2e-5 and batch size of 32

results.claim: Supervised Self-Notes beat Scratchpad on OOD Algorithmic (101-200 statements) with GPT-2.
results.setup: GPT-2 base fine-tuned, Algorithmic task, OOD 101-200 statements, supervised notes, mean ± std

results.claim: Toy-Story 4-hop OOD (trained on 1/2-hop): Self-Notes vs Scratchpad vs Vanilla.
results.setup: GPT-2, Toy-Story, train 10k 1-2 hop, test 4-hop, supervised

results.claim: Scratchpad falls below Vanilla on OOD Algorithmic because it copies the context and exceeds GPT-2's 1024-token limit.
results.quote: Scratchpad fails at most examples since the context length exceeds the maximum length of GPT-2 (1024 tokens).

results.claim: Boolean Variable OOD (9-19 statements) gain is small.
results.setup: GPT-2, Boolean Variable chain-like split, train 3-8, test 9-19
results.table: Table 2, row Boolean Variable 9-19*, column Self-Notes

results.claim: Chess Piecetype OOD (>=81 moves): Self-Notes roughly equal to Scratchpad, both far above Vanilla.
results.setup: GPT-2, 200k train samples up to 80 moves
results.table: Table 2, row Chess Piecetype >=81*, column Self-Notes

results.claim: Chess Move OOD: Self-Notes slightly above Vanilla; Scratchpad worse.
results.setup: GPT-2, Chess Move exact match, >=81 moves
results.table: Table 2, row Chess Move >=81*, column Self-Notes

results.claim: Semi-supervised: 1% Self-Note supervision (100 samples) already beats Vanilla on Toy-Story; saturates near 25%.
results.quote: even Self-Note supervision using as little as 1% of the training set (100 samples), leads to performance gains over the Vanilla model

results.claim: Unsupervised Self-Notes on Toy-Story 4-hop with notes, boosting, multi-sample and finetune.
results.setup: GPT-2, 100k samples of 1-2 hop with no notes, boost B=5, multi-sample select most confident, finetune on generated notes

results.claim: Unsupervised 1-variable Algorithmic reaches near 100% with 20k samples.
results.quote: With 20k samples, the unsupervised Self-Notes method achieves near 100% accuracy, with a significant increase over the Vanilla model.

results.claim: Few-shot GPT-J (6B) on MultiArith: Self-Notes vs CoT vs Vanilla.
results.setup: GPT-J 6B, 8-shot from Wei et al., 600 MultiArith test samples

results.claim: Few-shot GPT-3 175B (text-davinci-003) on GSM8K: Self-Notes slightly above CoT.
results.setup: GPT-3 175B via API, 5-shot, 1319 test, notes only after '.', ',' '?'
Llama 2 70B, 8-shot prompt from Wei et al.

results.claim: 10k Self-Notes Toy-Story samples (~80k QA pairs) beat Vanilla given 1500% more samples.
results.quote: The Self-Notes model with 10k samples still vastly outperforms the Vanilla model with a 1500% increase in training samples

results.claim: Without notes at inference, a model trained with 100% Self-Notes collapses on OOD Algorithmic.
results.setup: GPT-2, train 100% notes, test no notes, Algorithmic 101-200

results.claim: Dummy tokens help only slightly on Chess Piecetype OOD; real note content matters more than extra compute.
results.setup: GPT-2, Chess Piecetype >=81 moves, dummy '_' between positions
results.table: Table 10, row Chess Piecetype, column Dummy
results.quote: suggesting that the content of the intermediate notes matters more than just the additional compute

limits: Supervised and few-shot variants need hand-written notes; same annotation burden as scratchpad/CoT (authors concede).
Only small GPT-2 fine-tuning for most tasks; mostly synthetic tasks.
GSM8K gain over CoT with GPT-3 is small (13.4 vs 11.4); used older davinci-003, not the stronger GPT-3 version of Wei et al.
Boolean Variable and Chess Piecetype gains over Scratchpad are within noise.
No code release stated; optimizer, seeds count, decoding not stated.
Authors leave RL discovery of notes and out-of-the-box note generation to future work.
Dummy-token ablation: note content matters more than extra compute, but position (mid-context) also helps.
